steps: A pair needs the same sole design and opposite feet.
Turn each sole in your mind until its toe points up, then check which side its big toe is on.
Group by design, then pair lefts with rights.
There are 3 matched pairs.
qs.trap: Pairing two soles of the same foot.

steps: Work out the rule from X: how do its edges become surfaces?
Check the rule gives 11 for X.
Count Y's edges and apply the rule.
Y gives 22.
qs.trap: Skipping the check with X.

steps: Each pair hugs once: 15 × 14 ÷ 2 = 105 hugs.
Each person gives 2 gifts to each of 14 others: 15 × 14 × 2 = 420 gifts.
Difference: 420 − 105 = 315.
The key also accepts −315 (hugs minus gifts).

steps: Count the small tetrahedra on one face.
There are 4 faces, but pieces on edges and corners belong to more than one face.
Subtract the shared pieces so each is counted once.
The total is 44.
qs.trap: Multiplying one face by 4 without removing shared edge pieces.

steps: Use the examples to find the value of each colour and the base.
Convert the two numbers in the multiplication to decimal.
Multiply.
The result is 18.
qs.trap: Multiplying the colour codes directly. Convert to decimal first.

steps: List all 36 products of 1 to 6 with 1 to 6.
Remove repeats: 6 = 1 × 6 = 2 × 3, and so on.
That is 18 results.

steps: Draw all three engravings on one square.
Count small triangles first, then larger ones made of several pieces.
Use any symmetry to check.
The total is 20.
qs.trap: Counting each sheet separately. Lines from different sheets make new triangles.

steps: Each block goes back and forth in its own track, reversing at the walls.
Write each block's position at every second.
Look for the first time all three positions match.
That happens at 7 seconds.
qs.trap: Forgetting that blocks reverse at the walls.

steps: The common part is bounded by faces of both prisms.
From the side view, see which faces of each prism enclose the overlap.
Count each bounding face once.
The intersection has 9 surfaces.
qs.trap: Describing the union. The question asks for the shared part only.

steps: Use symmetry: count the cubes in one part and multiply.
Count the layers from top to bottom, row by row.
Include the hidden centre cubes (no hollows).
The total is 57.
qs.trap: Missing hidden inner cubes.

steps: Count the original flat faces.
The drill hole adds one curved surface (a tunnel wall).
Check whether the hole splits any face into separate pieces.
The total is 10.
qs.trap: Counting the two hole openings as surfaces.

steps: BQ runs along the diagonals of the hinged rhombi.
Each diagonal is proportional to cos(half the angle).
150 root 6 × root 1.5 = 150 root 9 = 450.
qs.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 236 112" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="4" y="4" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="19" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">Each rhombus diagonal = 2 × stick × cos(half the angle)</text><rect x="4" y="30" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="45" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">At 90°: cos 45° = 0.707; at 60°: cos 30° = 0.866</text><rect x="4" y="56" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#DCE6F7" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="71" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="600" fill="#0A2560" text-anchor="start">BQ grows by 0.866 ÷ 0.707 = root 1.5</text><rect x="4" y="82" width="228" height="22" rx="3" fill="#FFE3CF" stroke="none" stroke-width="0"/><text x="10" y="97" font-family="Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif" font-size="7.8" font-weight="700" fill="#FF6B0A" text-anchor="start">150 root 6 × root 1.5 = 150 × 3 = 450</text></svg>
qs.trap: Scaling by the angle (60/90). Use the cosine of half the angle.

steps: Use equations i to iii to decode each symbol.
Check each decoded equation is correct arithmetic.
Decode equation iv and work out the answer.
The answer is 399, with 9 appearing twice.
qs.trap: Guessing symbols without checking every equation.

steps: Look for curved black parts that fit into white gaps.
Move pieces to make simple shapes.
Compare with the square's area of 256.
The black area is 96 cm².
qs.trap: Calculating every curve separately.

steps: An equilateral triangle's side = 2 root 3 × its inradius = 2 root 3 × root 3 = 6.
The two triangles cut each side into three equal parts of 2.
The star border has 12 such edges.

qs.trap: Adding both triangles' full perimeters (36). The inner parts are not on the border.

steps: Compare the same digit across numbers: 1, 0 and 9 appear often.
Look at stroke endings, curves and widths.
One number has a digit drawn differently.
That number is 1190.
qs.trap: Comparing different digits. Compare the same digit across numbers.

steps: Count faces visible in the first view.
Add faces visible only in the second view.
Hidden surfaces are flat, so a hidden region counts as one face.
The key accepts 22 or 23, as one face can be read either way.
qs.trap: Counting the same face from both views twice.

steps: Compare each piece on the left with its partner on the right.
Mark pieces that already mirror each other.
Count the pieces that need changing.
The fewest is 9.
qs.trap: Moving both pieces of a mismatched pair. Moving one is enough.

steps: The circle's diameter 14 root 2 is the diagonal of a square of side 14.
Each semicircle sits on a side of that square, radius 7.
Petals = four semicircles − the square = 4 × ½ × 22/7 × 49 − 196.

qs.trap: Adding the four semicircles without removing the overlap with the square.

steps: Count each colour of cow in the sketch carefully.
Watch for overlapping cows.
Multiply each count by its milk and add.
The total is 160 litres.
qs.trap: Missing a cow hidden behind another.

steps: A tile fits with copies of itself when every bump matches a dent on the opposite side.
Check top against bottom and left against right.
Shifted rows are allowed.
C and D tile.
qs.trap: Choosing by looks.

B: Pandit Nikhil Banerjee and Ustad Vilayat Khan: sitar. True.
C: Ali Akbar Khan and Amjad Ali Khan play sarod; only L. Subramaniam plays violin. False.
D: Ravi Shankar played sitar; Hariprasad Chaurasia plays flute. False.

steps: Note the profile's fold lines and lengths.
Fold each segment in your mind.
Check lengths and angles match each option.
B, C and D can be folded.
qs.trap: Ignoring segment lengths.

steps: A structure passes if some view of it fits inside the L.
Check each structure's front, side and top outlines.
Any orientation is allowed.
All four can pass.
qs.trap: Checking only one orientation.

steps: Statement (i): anyone who beats me in one item beats me in all.
Statement (ii): anyone below me in one item is also below me in another.
Check each farmer's bars against every other farmer.
Only Neela (C) can make one of them truthfully.
qs.trap: Checking against one other farmer only. "Everyone" means all of them.

steps: A closed route using every road once needs every city to have an even number of roads.
Count the roads at each city.
One odd city rules a network out.
B and D pass.
qs.trap: Trying routes by trial.

steps: Count the squares to cover; the tile size must divide it.
Check the tile can turn corners and fill around the gap.
Try a full layout.
C works; the key also accepts C, D.
qs.trap: Checking only the area. The shape must also fit.

steps: Tina brought the pen and gave it away.
Biju says he received his gift from the one who gave to the ball-giver, which is Suresh. So Suresh gave to Biju, and Biju gave away the ball.
The swap is a loop: Suresh to Biju, Biju to Tina, Tina to Suresh. Tina gets the ball and Suresh gets the pen.
Biju gets Suresh's book. A, C and D are true.
qs.trap: Assuming Tina wanted the book. Work from the facts, not the wishes.

steps: A regular hexagon needs six equal sides in the cut.
A cube cut through the middle at a slant gives one.
Check which blocks have enough faces at the right angles.
A and B can.
qs.trap: Accepting any six-sided cut. The sides must be equal.

steps: Find the smallest repeating tile in each pattern.
Check that every tile is the same, just rotated.
Two different tile designs rule a pattern out.
A and C use one tile.
qs.trap: Missing a second tile type hidden in the pattern.

steps: Arunachal Pradesh (about 83,700 km²) is larger than Kerala (38,900). True.
Punjab (50,400) is smaller than Assam (78,400). False.
Chhattisgarh (135,200) is larger than Jharkhand (79,700). True.
West Bengal (88,800) is larger than Uttarakhand (53,500). True.

steps: Find the net change from P to Q: a mirror image, turned.
Work through each sequence with a simple letter like F.
B and D give the same result as Q.
A and C give different results.
qs.trap: Doing the steps in the wrong order. Order matters with flips.

steps: Identify each bird from its features.
Recall which are found in India (peacock, hornbill, kingfisher and others).
Rule out birds from other continents.
A, B and D are native.
qs.trap: Guessing from colour alone.

steps: Compare letter construction: serifs, contrast, the shape of a, g, e.
Ignore size and colour.
Find options matching every feature.
B and D match.
qs.trap: Choosing by weight.

steps: Light passes where openings in both frames line up.
Move the blue frame as its hinge or pivot allows.
Check whether the openings can line up to make the pattern.
A and C can.
qs.trap: Moving frames in ways their hinges do not allow.

steps: All the tools are levers: they share a working principle. A true.
Not all of them cut fabric. B false.
One has a spring to open it again; at least one has a nut-cracking part. C true.
Not three of them crack nuts. D false.
qs.trap: Assuming all scissors-like tools cut fabric.

steps: Follow the folds step by step to see where each printed page ends up.
Write the final page order.
Check each statement against it.
A, B and D are true.
qs.trap: Assuming pages end in printed order.

steps: A: one sock white = 10/20 = 50%. True.
B: two socks the same colour = 2 × 10/20 × 9/19 = 47%, not 50%. False.
C: with 3 socks, two must match (only 2 colours): 100%, higher than 47%. True.
D: with 4 socks it is also 100%, not higher than with 3. False.

steps: Lifting means raising the packet against gravity, then lowering it.
Sliding on a level or downhill surface needs little effort.
Compare each pair of actions.
B and D are true.
qs.trap: Ignoring the bin heights.

steps: List the four instruments: tabla, sitar, harmonium, sarod. Each group takes two, each instrument goes to two groups.
Mizrabs play tabla, so not sitar; Frets play sitar, so not tabla.
Mizrabs and Dictions share nothing, nor do Frets and Scripts; Dictions avoid harmonium.
Every arrangement that fits has Mizrabs on tabla and harmonium, Dictions on sitar and sarod, Scripts on tabla, and Frets never on tabla. All four statements are true.
qs.trap: Stopping before every clue is used.

steps: The left side writes Indian state names in Sinhala script. Use the examples like a codebook.
Gujarat gives the symbol for "raa" (the third letter in its word).
Maharashtra has "raa" in the middle: "Ma-haa-raa-shtra".
Only D has the "raa" symbol in the middle of a word that starts differently from the other options: D.
qs.trap: Matching by word length. Match a sound you can decode.

steps: Compare construction: serifs, contrast, letter shapes.
Ignore size.
Find the full match.
A matches.
qs.trap: Choosing by weight.

steps: Look at the shapes cut by the four edges of the white hole.
Each cut shape must continue smoothly into the missing piece: same outline, same fill pattern.
Check one edge at a time and cross out any option that breaks a shape.
B continues every edge: B.
qs.trap: Judging by overall look. Check the edges one by one.

steps: An envelope is a square with four flaps folded in.
Each cut goes through every layer it crosses.
Unfold flap by flap, mirroring cuts.
B shows the result.
qs.trap: Forgetting cuts go through several layers.

steps: Each fold mirrors lines onto the other half.
Combine the original and mirrored lines.
Compare with the motif.
A makes it.
qs.trap: Moving lines without mirroring.

steps: A beam tilted downwards drops further the farther it travels.
The middle of each wall is nearest the centre, so the beam hits it highest.
The corners are farthest, so the beam hits them lowest.
So the path dips at each corner and rises in the middle of each wall: A.
qs.trap: Drawing a level line on every wall.

steps: Each outline segment in a view is an edge of some face.
Build the simplest solid matching all three views.
Count its faces.
The fewest is 14.
qs.trap: Choosing the most complex solid.

steps: When running, the arm opposite the forward leg swings forward.
The body leans slightly forward.
One foot is off the ground.
C shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a pose with the same arm and leg forward.

steps: Note which hand holds the bat and where each foot is.
Turn the figure 90° in your mind.
Check the bat angle.
C matches.
qs.trap: Swapping the leading foot.

steps: A mirror swaps left and right as seen by the viewer.
Her raised hand appears on the other side.
Check details like the hair parting.
C is correct.
qs.trap: Keeping left and right the same.

steps: Light from below brightens the chin, nostrils and underside of the brows.
Shadows fall upward on the face.
The top of the head is dark.
B shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing normal lighting from above.

steps: Note each part's position from above.
Check heights don't matter; only outlines.
Compare details.
D matches.
qs.trap: Mixing up the front and back.

steps: Pour 8 › 5, then 5 › 3, then 3 › 8: now 6, 2, 0.
Pour 5 › 3, then 8 › 5: now 1, 5, 2.
Pour 5 › 3 (fills it): 1, 4, 3. Pour 3 › 8: 4, 4, 0.
Seven pourings.

steps: If P tells the truth, Q lies (Q says P lies). Then R (who backs Q) lies too: two liars.
So P must be the liar.
Then Q is right; R and S agree with Q and R.
Exactly one liar: P.

steps: Every line entering the gap must continue across it.
Note each line's angle at the gap edge.
Find the piece that continues them all.
A does.
qs.trap: Choosing a piece that matches most but not all lines.

steps: Folding backwards hides the folded parts behind.
Turning over shows the back, with the folded sleeves now on top.
Track the sleeves and collar through each fold.
C is correct.
qs.trap: Folding forwards.

steps: The punch goes through every layer of the roll.
Holes repeat once per turn, with spacing growing outward.
Holes alternate direction where the roll's sides face opposite ways.
D shows this.
qs.trap: Expecting evenly spaced identical holes.

steps: It is the same solid in every frame, turning a little more each time.
Pick one feature, such as the small cube or the notch, and follow how it moves from frame to frame.
Continue the turn by one more step.
C shows the next position: C.
qs.trap: Choosing a view that matches the shape but turns the wrong way.

steps: A tetrahedron has 4 triangular faces.
Match the faces of the two pieces so that edges line up: point to point.
Check the given letter pairs.
af, bg, ci: option B.
qs.trap: Joining faces that do not match in shape.

steps: Two half-turns about different axes equal one half-turn about the third axis (x).
So the result is the object turned 180° about x.
Track one feature.
A shows this.
qs.trap: Doing only one rotation.

steps: From inside you see the sign mirrored: south-west inside means south-east outside.
Falling flips the sign upside down about its bottom edge.
Undoing that flip turns south-east into north-east.
Originally it pointed north-east.

qs.trap: Doing only one of the two flips.

steps: The cone is wider (12) than the cube (10) at the base but narrower (6) at the top.
Near the base, cone material sticks out beyond the cube's sides; above the cube (height 10) the cone continues.
So what remains is a ring of four curved pieces at the bottom plus the cone top above 10.
A shows this.
qs.trap: Forgetting the part of the cone above the cube.

steps: With the same perimeter, rounder shapes have more area.
A circle holds the most; long thin shapes the least.
Rank the four shapes by area.
Jai gets Q (second) and Jaspreet S (smallest).
qs.trap: Ranking by length instead of area.

steps: The river carries the crocodile downstream while it swims.
So targets downstream are easier to reach.
Add the drift to each route and compare times.
B is quickest.
qs.trap: Ignoring the current.

steps: Find the rule linking the numbers.
Check it on every group.
Apply it to the gap.
The answer is 24.
qs.trap: Building a rule from one group.

steps: Pick a distinctive corner on the white shape.
Rotate each black shape to line it up.
Mirror images do not count.
C matches.
qs.trap: Accepting a mirror image.

steps: Count the cubes of each colour you can see.
The other pieces are shown separately; the red one fills the rest.
27 minus the other pieces gives the red count and shape.
B is the red piece.
qs.trap: Forgetting hidden cubes.

steps: Green and orange circles at the ends of the rows stay fixed.
Follow each yellow and each cyan circle on its own: each moves one place along its own path every frame.
Move every coloured circle one more step.
Only B puts all of them in the right places: B.
qs.trap: Tracking all colours at once. Follow one circle at a time.

steps: Arun is the anaesthetist and works with everyone except intensive care.
Teams: neurosurgeon + orthopaedic + Arun; gynaecologist + paediatrician + Arun.
Jaya and Sushama are in one team; Sudhir and Dilip in the other.
Rama is left over: intensive care.

steps: Fast motion blurs the cabins along their path.
The hub stays sharp; the rim blurs most.
Blur trails follow the direction of motion.
D shows this.
qs.trap: Choosing a sharp photo.

steps: In each row the square turns a little further from left to right.
The thin lines inside move with the square, so they keep their place relative to its sides.
In the last row, continue both the turn and the line positions one more step.
D fits both: D.
qs.trap: Watching only the turn and forgetting the inner lines.

steps: Track one feature through each frame.
Note the turning direction.
Put the frames in order.
B is right.
qs.trap: Mixing up the direction.

steps: Identify each craft by its style and material.
Match each to its home country.
Check which option lists all four.
C: India, Russia, Japan, Turkey.
qs.trap: Matching just one craft.

steps: Look at the shapes: hammered bars, holes, bends and spirals.
Hand-worked iron is forged (hammered hot), then bent, punched and twisted.
Casting would leave a moulded look; drilling is a machine process.
A: forging, bending, punching, twisting.
qs.trap: Choosing casting for any metal object.

steps: Stability depends on a low centre of gravity and a wide base.
Count the visible parts of each chair.
Check each statement.
C: P is most stable; S has the fewest visible parts.
qs.trap: Judging stability by looks.

steps: Look for features: a nut-cracking jaw, the grip, any can opener.
Think about how it was made: wood is turned and drilled, not cast.
Check each statement: 1 fits; 2 adds a can opener that is not there; 3 mentions casting.
A: 1 is true, 2 and 3 are false.
qs.trap: Accepting a statement because half of it is true. Both halves must be true.

steps: The first mirror copies it below the x-axis.
The second copies both pieces across the y-axis.
The result has four parts, mirror images of each other.
D shows this.
qs.trap: Rotating instead of mirroring.

steps: Fold step by step.
Each fold halves or quarters the shape.
Track the edges.
B is right.
qs.trap: Skipping a fold.

steps: Fold the net.
Find which face points towards X.
Check how its cut-out is turned.
D is right.
qs.trap: Using the wrong face.

steps: Grip force is strongest when fingers and thumb wrap fully and oppose each other.
More skin contact and a closed fist give more force.
Compare the grips.
D is the strongest.
qs.trap: Choosing a fingertip grip.

steps: Try single pieces, pairs, triples and all four.
Check each combination for straight outer edges and right angles.
Count the ones that work.
Five combinations.
qs.trap: Missing combinations of three pieces.

steps: The neck curves in an S-shape to hold the head.
Vertebrae are larger near the body.
Compare each option.
B is most correct.
qs.trap: Choosing a straight neck.

steps: Find how each triangle relates to the next (for example, joining midpoints halves the side).
Each step multiplies the area by the square of the side ratio.
Multiply over all steps.
The ratio is 16.
qs.trap: Using the side ratio instead of its square.

steps: A jump: crouch, push off, stretch in the air, land, crouch.
Find where the gap is in that cycle.
Choose the frame that fits.
C fits.
qs.trap: Choosing a frame from the wrong phase.

steps: The two figures are halves of one hexagon. Put one on top of the other without turning either.
Navy and red pieces come from the first figure. Tan, green and grey come from the second.
Check that every coloured piece stays in the same place and direction.
Only A matches all the pieces: A.
qs.trap: Turning one half before combining. The halves fit as drawn.
